claim: A prospective, preregistered tournament found frontier LLMs ranked 30 live Kickstarter ventures better than 346 experienced managers and 3 MBA investors (best LLM rho 0.74 vs best human 0.45, crowd 0.19). Replication on 26 projects was LLM-only and gave lower absolute correlations (model-rank consistency about 0.54). One domain, single calls, no scaffold or token matching (d15).
agent_test: Run our agent on the same pairwise ranking task on fresh ventures at equal tokens against a plain single-call baseline.

claim: Averaging models or adding a human did not beat the best single LLM (Gemini+Expert 0.67 < 0.74; Gemini+GPT-5 Mini 0.77, +0.03 not significant). Same-family models correlate 0.80-0.97 so same-family panels add little.
agent_test: Compare K independent samples of our agent vs one sample at equal tokens on the ranking task; measure gain from mixing model families.

claim: LLM Delphi panels track benchmark ground truth (r 0.91-0.98, MAE 4.5-6.1 pp) only when benchmark and agent identity are supplied; with that evidence hidden, r falls to 0.30, -0.22, -0.40. The skill is in the evidence, not the panel process. The paper has no round-by-round data or no-feedback arm (d13).
agent_test: Ablate evidence in our agent scenario step; compare against a single call with the same evidence at equal tokens.

claim: LLM panels show conformity and compressed spread: panelists cite the panel mean far more than humans (humans 0.6% vs GPT-5.1 +45.4 pts), numeric convergence over rounds, and in multi-agent value deliberation single-model panels collapse to one option (70.9% first-choice; 46.1% with mixed models).
agent_test: Measure spread before and after feedback rounds in our agent; test independent drafts then merge vs shared-feedback rounds at equal tokens.

claim: Choice of base model moves estimates more than persona prompts (persona 2.4 pp vs model 4.8 pp; after mediation 0.5 vs 4.4). Heterogeneous models reduce artificial consensus. Persona variety on one model is a weak diversity source.
agent_test: Compare persona-diverse single-model vs model-diverse panels at equal tokens on a scenario-generation task; score distinct-branch count.

claim: LLM-run Delphi output varies by run: themes in Bertolotti and Mari appear in some of 12 runs and not others (e.g. fragmentation 7 of 12), and the Soleimani repeat run differed per scenario while agreeing in aggregate.
agent_test: Repeat our scenario step 5 times; report theme recall across runs and aggregate stability.

claim: In LLM macro stress scenarios severity is set by the prompt, not the model (prompt variant partial eta-sq 0.87 GPT, about 0.40 Llama); removing severity bands made recession 1.6 pp milder. The small open model was 4-7x more dispersed and contradicted its own stated changes in 90% of cases.
agent_test: Check whether our agent scenario severity follows an explicit anchor in the prompt; test with and without severity bands.

claim: Narrative severity and numeric severity are weakly linked in LLM scenarios (association near zero in severe and systemic tiers); a story can read as catastrophe while carrying a mild number. Retrieval and news changed little once prompts fixed macro anchors.
agent_test: Add a text-to-number consistency check step; count scenarios failing it at equal tokens.

claim: The 2009 US bank stress test (SCAP) used a baseline and a more adverse scenario on 19 BHCs: about $600B two-year losses, $185B capital needed, 10 of 19 short. The market learned from it only at the results release, not at the announcement or method events.
agent_test: Not directly agent-testable; use as design pattern: disclose scenario assumptions and outputs, score whether revealing results changes decisions.

claim: Delphi in human studies: a vote-count review reports Delphi beat statistical groups 12 to 2 and interacting groups 5 to 1 (Rowe and Wright, snippet only); one business case gave 3-4% error vs 10-15% quantitative (Basu and Schroeder via Wikipedia). Evidence is thin and second-hand.
agent_test: Compare Delphi-style rounds against independent averaging at equal tokens on a forecasting set.

claim: General morphological analysis shrinks a large option space by pairwise cross-consistency checks: example 4x4x4x3x3x4 = 2,304 configurations; the original 10-parameter field exceeded 500,000. Pairwise judgments between conditions suit batch LLM labelling.
agent_test: Build a morphological box for a design task; have the agent label pairwise consistency; compare coverage of valid configurations vs free brainstorming at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM study tests Kahn-style stories, Berger La Prospective, or LLM-run morphological analysis directly; this rests on small negative searches. Gap search again found none (d11); the one story-style test (a scripted narrative prompt) hurt Brier for 11 of 12 models (d05).
agent_test: Run our own test: Kahn-style story vs branching scenarios vs plain answer on a foresight set with scored outcomes.

claim: Agents running Futures Wheels broaden coverage: 86-110 consequences per run condensed to 27-47 unique risks, theme similarity above 0.95 across runs, agent risks rated more systemic (experts 93%) than human-only lists (24-63%).
agent_test: Compare consequence-tree breadth and expert-rated systemic share vs a single-pass list at equal tokens.

claim: GPT-4 scenario pairs (without and with a policy) were rated plausible (3.94) and policy-sensitive (severity change -0.38, p<0.001, n=234 raters).
agent_test: Generate paired counterfactual scenarios and check rater-sensitive severity shift.

claim: Delphi-style feedback and self-confrontation failed on 8B models: counter-argument exposure caused capitulation, two rounds compounded sycophantic flips, self re-reading gave zero vote changes in 10 runs.
agent_test: Test critique-feedback rounds on a small model and our agent; count flips to wrong answers.

claim: LLM estimates diverge from human experts on quantities and long horizons: quantities lower by up to 70% (probabilities within 6%), non-monotonic with task difficulty; ice-sheet medians about half the human value at 2050 high-warming (65 vs 120 mm).
agent_test: Check monotonicity of our agent estimates across difficulty levels.

claim: Kahn scenario work (escalation ladder 16 to 44 steps; Year 2000 list of 100 innovations; Japan-passes-US by 1990) was narrative and never scored for accuracy in the sources read; all from Wikipedia.
agent_test: Score historical Kahn predictions against outcomes (needs primary text).

claim: A weighted persona panel with grounding tracked human ratings better than one judge (r 0.922 vs 0.716); most gain came from grounding and panel, not discussion. Task was UI rating, not forecasting.
agent_test: Ablate grounding vs discussion in our agent evaluation step.

claim: The early-1980s Shell review reportedly found weak implementation came from decisions after scenarios, not scenarios themselves.
agent_test: None; organisational claim.

claim: Feedback rounds in LLM forecasting give small, fragile gains. One round among three different frontier models cut log loss 0.501 to 0.481 (p 0.017) in one of four cells, with none for same-model groups. In a Delphi-style agent system, 2 rounds beat 1 (Brier 0.178 vs 0.206) and 3 rounds were worse (0.196), mainly from sharing rationales. Neither study matched tokens against independent samples plus averaging.
agent_test: Arm A: K independent samples averaged. Arm B: K samples plus one rationale-sharing round. Same total calls, scored by Brier on resolved questions.

claim: A story-framed forecasting prompt did not beat a direct range-first prompt: a scripted narrative prompt gave higher (worse) median Brier for 11 of 12 models on 334 questions (o3 0.1985 vs 0.1352). This is not Kahn-style branching, so branch-then-probability is still untested.
agent_test: Compare plain probability vs scenario branches with stated weights then combined, on the same resolved questions at equal tokens.

claim: Cheap numeric consistency checks catch LLM scenario failures that plausibility rules miss (requiring both levels and changes, reconciled to a fixed baseline), but they do not set severity. Authors advise prescribing the severity path and using the LLM for narrative only.
agent_test: Add a text-to-number reconciliation step to scenario output; measure contradiction rate before and after on 100 scenarios.

claim: Primary evidence for the traditions' own forecast accuracy was not recovered: RAND blocked Dalkey and Helmer 1963 and Sackman 1974, Rowe and Wright 1999 full text was blocked, and no hit-rate count for Kahn, Shell or La Prospective was found. Shell evidence is anecdotal and mostly from Shell; an early-1980s audit blamed post-scenario decisions.
agent_test: Treat the traditions as idea sources only, not as validated forecasters.

claim: No evidence yet that scenario-severity anchoring improves agent decisions, that heterogeneous models beat persona panels on accuracy at equal tokens, or that the Kickstarter ranking result holds in other domains or for scaffolds. These stay open (d02, d04, d15, d16).
agent_test: Run the three tests listed in the critique gap list at equal tokens.
